dimensions.assessment: Affects communities, property owners, and tribal governments along the approximately 2,400-mile alignment from Chicago to Santa Monica.
dimensions.evidence: extending along a route of approximately 2,400 miles from Chicago, Illinois, to Santa Monica, California

dimensions.assessment: Designates an official historic trail under administration of the Secretary of the Interior, explicitly barring eminent domain, condemnation, and new permit requirements.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of the Interior may not use eminent domain or condemnation... shall not subject the Route 66 National Historic Trail... to any other Federal laws... requiring a Federal permit

dimensions.assessment: Does not specify federal appropriations or funding amounts for trail management.
Amends the National Trails System Act to add a specific historic trail designation with explicit limitations on land acquisition and federal authority.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the National Trails System Act to designate the Route 66 National Historic Trail, and for other purposes.

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for the Department of the Interior to oversee the trail.
importance_detail.rationale: Designates Route 66 as a National Historic Trail across approximately 2,400 miles, with specific restrictions preventing eminent domain or new buffer zones.
